subject: chemistry
title: Energetics & Thermochemistry Adventure 1: Enthalpy and calorimetry
welcome_lead: Today you'll measure enthalpy with a calorimeter using q = mcΔT.
meta_desc: Chemistry — enthalpy, calorimetry q=mcΔT, exothermic/endothermic, standard conditions.
final_note: You learned ΔH = q at constant p, q = mcΔT, exo means -ΔH (releases heat), endo +ΔH (absorbs).

concepts.def: Energy to raise 1 g by 1 K

walkthroughs.body_html:
If bond making releases more energy than bond breaking, the reaction is exothermic (ΔH negative).

Examples: combustion (-2877 kJ/mol for octane), neutralisation, respiration.

Endothermic: absorbs energy. Photosynthesis, decomposition of CaCO₃ → CaO + CO₂ (+178 kJ/mol).

Heat transferred:

q = m × c × ΔT

m in g, c in J g⁻¹ K⁻¹ (water = 4.18), ΔT in K or °C (size same).

Lab: burn 0.46 g ethanol; heats 200 g water from 20°C to 35°C.
q = 200 × 4.18 × 15 = 12,540 J.
n(ethanol) = 0.46/46 = 0.01 mol.
ΔH_c = -12.54/0.01 = -1254 kJ/mol (lit: -1367; difference = heat loss).

Symbol ⦵: standard conditions (): 100 kPa, stated T (usually 298 K), 1 mol dm⁻³ solutions.

Key standard enthalpies:
- ΔH_c⦵ combustion: 1 mol burnt in O₂.
- ΔH_f⦵ formation: 1 mol from elements in standard states.
- ΔH_n⦵ neutralisation: 1 mol H₂O formed from acid+base.

mcqs.q: Specific heat of water (J g⁻¹ K⁻¹):
Why can an endothermic reaction still be spontaneous?
options: If the entropy increase (TΔS) is large enough to outweigh the positive ΔH, ΔG can still be negative.
Hydration enthalpy is the same for all ions because water molecules are identical.
All endothermic reactions are spontaneous at room temperature.
Endothermic reactions are never spontaneous because they require energy input.

mcqs.q: Why is the hydration enthalpy of a small, highly charged ion very exothermic?
options: Hydration enthalpy only depends on the size of the ion, not its charge.
Small/highly charged ions form strong ion-dipole attractions with water molecules, releasing a large amount of energy.
Hydration enthalpy is the same for all ions because water molecules are identical.
ΔH becomes zero because the change cancels out.

mcqs.q: When you reverse a reaction in a Hess cycle, what happens to ΔH?
options: Hydration enthalpy is the same for all ions because water molecules are identical.
ΔH stays the same because it's the same reaction.
Its sign reverses — if the forward reaction is +100 kJ/mol, the reverse is -100 kJ/mol.
ΔH becomes zero because the change cancels out.
